To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the cytosolically exposed region of the attractin-like protein ALP binds to the intracellular tail of the melanocortin 4 receptor, and this interaction may modulate the receptor's function.
the cytosolically exposed C-terminal region of the melanocortin 4 receptor interacts directly with the cytosolic domain of an attractin family protein.
the cytoskeletal attractin-like protein ALP binds directly to the C-terminal tail of the melanocortin 4 receptor and this interaction is required for efficient MC4R signalling in vitro and in vivo.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the molecular mechanisms that regulate food intake and energy balance, in particular, with the identification of new targets for the development of anti-obesity drugs.
the molecular basis of obesity, and in particular with the role of attractins in the regulation of energy balance and the pathogenesis of obesity.
the identification and characterization of novel proteins that are involved in the regulation of melanocortin function and, in particular, the development of obesity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the attractin family of proteins may be involved in the modulation of melanocortin function and thus play a role in the control of body weight.
the MC4R is a target of attractin, and that attractin is a target for agouti.
the attractin family is a new player in the field of energy balance and obesity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a protein, ALP (attractin-like protein), which binds to the C-terminal end of the melanocortin receptors, MC3R and MC4R.
attractin and its homologues are a family of proteins that can influence melanocortins and their receptors in multiple ways.
the MC4R is the key player in the regulation of energy homeostasis.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the melanocortin system is much more complex than we previously imagined, with the possibility that attractin family proteins play a role in the regulation of appetite in both normal and obese individuals.
attractin and attractin-like proteins are likely to have important roles in regulating the activity of the MC4R and other G-protein-couple receptors.
attractin-like proteins are important for melanocortin signaling, and may have a role in obesity.
